Test Description: Verifies PCIe device enumeration on dual PCIe controllers. The test initializes the system, performs link training for x4 lane configuration, programs cache coherency control registers, and polls link status registers until both controllers report link-up. Under Root Complex mode, the test reads the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to obtain the Vendor ID, writes to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO space, memory space, and bus master access, and programs memory base addresses. System-level configuration registers are set. Cache coherency is subsequently disabled. BAR sizing is performed on both PCIe slave interfaces by writing all-ones to BAR0_REG, BAR1_REG, SEC_LAT_TIMER_SUB_BUS_SEC_BUS_PRI_BUS_REG, SEC_STAT_IO_LIMIT_IO_BASE_REG, MEM_LIMIT_MEM_BASE_REG, and PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG, reading back to determine BAR sizes, then programming actual base addresses and verifying. The test polls a completion status register until the expected completion value is observed.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Initialize the system by writing to the system control register to clear its state. 2. Perform PCIe link training for x4 lane width on the applicable controller mode. 3. Program the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register on both PCIe controllers to enable cache coherency. 4. Wait for the coherency configuration to take effect. 5. Poll the link status register on PCIe controller 0 until link-up is confirmed. 6. Poll the link status register on PCIe controller 1 until link-up is confirmed. 7. In Root Complex mode, read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to obtain the device Vendor ID. 8. Write to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO space, memory space, and bus master access. 9. Program memory base addresses for both controllers. 10. Configure system-level protection and control registers. 11. Disable cache coherency by clearing the relevant bit fields in the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register on both controllers. 12. Perform BAR sizing on both PCIe slave interfaces. 13. Program actual base address values and read back to verify. 14. Poll the completion status register until the expected completion value is observed. 15. End the test upon successful completion.
Impacted Registers: COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF; TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG; TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG; BAR0_REG; BAR1_REG; SEC_LAT_TIMER_SUB_BUS_SEC_BUS_PRI_BUS_REG; SEC_STAT_IO_LIMIT_IO_BASE_REG; MEM_LIMIT_MEM_BASE_REG; PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when: (1) Both PCIe controllers achieve link-up. (2) The TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG returns a valid Vendor ID. (3) BAR sizing returns valid size information. (4) Programmed BAR values are read back successfully. (5) The completion status register returns the expected completion value.
Remarks: The testcase operates on dual PCIe controllers with both slave interfaces. Link training mode is selected via compile-time defines. Polling is used for link-up detection and final test completion. Several system-level registers could not be mapped to named registers in the specification.

Feature: PCIe DMA Write and Read Transfer
Test Description: Verifies PCIe DMA write and read data transfers across four DMA channels on a PCIe controller. The test initializes the system, performs link training for x4 lane configuration, and polls the link status register until link-up is confirmed. The Vendor ID is read from TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, and the TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG is written to enable IO space, memory space, and bus master access. Source memory is preloaded with known data patterns. DMA write and read interrupt masks are unmasked by writing to DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF. For each of four DMA channels, the write channel is programmed and the DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF register is written to trigger the transfer. The interrupt handler reads DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF, and writes to DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF to clear the interrupts.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Initialize the system by writing to the system control register. 2. Perform PCIe link training for x4 lane width. 3. Poll the link status register until link-up is confirmed. 4. Read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to obtain the Vendor ID. 5. Write to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO, memory, and bus master access. 6. Perform BAR and memory base programming. 7. Poll the completion status register. 8. Preload source memory with known data patterns. 9. Enable interrupts via GIC setup. 10. Unmask DMA interrupts by writing to DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF. 11. For each of four DMA write channels, program and trigger via DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF. 12. For each of four DMA read channels, program and trigger via DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF. 13. In the interrupt handler, read and clear DMA status registers. 14. End the test upon successful completion.
Impacted Registers: TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG; TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG; DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF; DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF; DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF; DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF; DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF; DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF; DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF; DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when: (1) The PCIe link achieves link-up. (2) The TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG returns a valid Vendor ID. (3) All four DMA write channel transfers complete via interrupt. (4) All four DMA read channel transfers complete via interrupt. (5) The interrupt handler correctly reads and clears DMA status registers. (6) The test completes with finish(0).
Remarks: The testcase operates on one of two PCIe controllers selected via compile-time defines. Four DMA write and four DMA read channels are exercised sequentially. Interrupt-driven completion is used. All DMA registers for the second PCIe controller could not be resolved.

Test Description: Verifies PCIe memory write and read operations through the PCIe slave interfaces on dual PCIe controllers. The test initializes the system, performs link training, programs cache coherency control registers, and polls the link status register until link-up is confirmed. Under Root Complex mode, the test reads the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, writes to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG, and performs BAR and memory base programming. Cache coherency is disabled. Memory write-read verification is performed through the PCIe slave interface at multiple memory addresses with known data patterns. The test polls a completion status register until the expected completion value is observed.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Initialize the system by writing to the system control register. 2. Perform PCIe link training for x4 lane width. 3. Program the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register on both controllers to enable cache coherency. 4. Wait for coherency configuration to take effect. 5. Poll the link status register until link-up is confirmed. 6. Read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to obtain the Vendor ID. 7. Write to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO, memory, and bus master access. 8. Perform BAR and memory base programming. 9. In Endpoint mode, perform EP-specific BAR programming. 10. Configure system-level protection registers. 11. Disable cache coherency. 12. Perform memory write-read verification at multiple addresses. 13. Poll the completion status register. 14. End the test upon successful completion.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when: (1) The PCIe link achieves link-up. (2) The TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG returns a valid Vendor ID. (3) Memory write-read operations complete successfully for all tested addresses and data patterns. (4) The completion status register returns the expected value.
Remarks: The testcase supports both Root Complex and Endpoint modes. In RC mode, three memory addresses are tested per controller. In EP mode, five BAR1 offsets are tested. Cache coherency is enabled before link-up and disabled before memory operations.

Test Description: Verifies PCIe register reset values and write-read integrity across multiple register groups on both PCIe controllers. The test checks that all DBI controller registers (MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF), SII interface registers, and PHY registers read their expected default values after reset. It then performs write-read verification by writing multiple test patterns and reading back to confirm data integrity. Write masks are applied for SII and PHY registers.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Read all DBI controller registers on both controllers and verify default reset values. 2. Read all SII interface registers and verify default reset values. 3. Write to the PHY reset control register to enable PHY access. 4. Read all PHY registers with alignment-based masking and verify defaults. 5. Write test patterns to all DBI controller registers (MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF). 6. Write test patterns with write masks to SII registers. 7. Write PHY-specific test patterns with write masks. 8. Read back all DBI registers and verify. 9. Read back SII registers and verify with write masks. 10. Read back PHY registers with alignment masking and verify. 11. Repeat for multiple test patterns. 12. Report pass if no mismatches; otherwise fail.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when: (1) All DBI registers read expected default values. (2) All SII registers read expected defaults. (3) All PHY registers read expected defaults. (4) Write-read verification passes for all test patterns on DBI registers. (5) Write-read verification passes for SII registers with write masks. (6) Write-read verification passes for PHY registers with alignment masking. (7) The test completes with finish(0) when no errors detected.
Remarks: The testcase does not perform link training. It directly accesses DBI, SII, and PHY registers. Write masks are applied for SII and PHY registers. PHY reads use alignment-based masking. Three test pattern iterations are performed. All SII and PHY registers could not be mapped to named registers in the specification.
